commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that an emf keeps flowing the whole time the magnet sits inside the coil.

fixIt.corrected: No change in flux, no emf: the magnet sitting still gives zero - only motion makes the meter kick.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state what the meter shows while the magnet sits perfectly still inside the coil, and why.

commonErrors.misconception: An emf flows as long as the magnet sits inside the coil.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks the statement that a steady voltage appears because the coil is full of flux.

fixIt.corrected: Zero: the flux is not changing, so no emf is induced
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence why a coil full of steady flux has no induced emf.

commonErrors.misconception: An emf flows as long as the magnet sits inside the coil.

modelAnswers.question: The flux through a 200-turn coil falls from 0.030 Wb to 0.010 Wb in 0.50 s. Calculate the induced emf, showing your working with Faraday's law.
A 50-turn coil has the flux through it increase by 0.012 Wb in 0.30 s. Calculate the induced emf.

nextSteps: Reteach the sitting-magnet trap from the paired notes trap before any further electromagnetism work: only a change in flux induces an emf.
Practise showing the flux change step explicitly whenever Faraday's law is used in a calculation.
strengths: Most of the class can compute the flux through a coil, such as 0.0080 Wb, from Phi = BA = 0.40 x 0.020 on the worksheet.
The class can state that electric field lines run from positive to negative and magnetic lines loop from N to S on the exit ticket.
